deepseek_columns.ai_commands: sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "sudo dmidecode -t 17 2>/dev/null | grep -iA1 \"Total Width\""
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL raw `dmidecode -t 17` output filtered to the `Total Width` value for that section (raw text, verbatim) so the user can diff against expected; judge correctness/persistence after reboot.

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES; captures width text without device identity, raw FFFFh handling or Data Width relationship.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; adds per-device width/ECC correlation and unknown sentinel handling but lowers capability for pending inputs.
historical_reviews.round_02: YES; retained the grep command and agent-direct execution framing, with operator target selection and judgment.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: No V3/V3.1 record exists for this variant.

original_test_intent: Verify that every Type 17 record reports the approved total transfer width in bits for its memory device, correctly represents Unknown with FFFFh, is not narrower than known Data Width, reflects the intended check-bit design and remains stable after reboot.
original_method: Capture complete raw Type 17 records, identify devices by locator/array/serial/population state, decode raw Total Width and Data Width including FFFFh, compare total/data/check-bit relationships with the approved module/ECC design and optional trusted SPD evidence, then repeat after reboot.
manual_activity: A user approves the width/ECC baseline and reboot plan. No DIMM or ECC-setting change is required.
required_inputs: Expected Total Width and Data Width per populated device class
Expected check-bit width or non-ECC equality rule
Policy for FFFFh Unknown and unpopulated Type 17 records
Stable device identity and optional trusted SPD mapping
Validated parser and approved reboot/OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Use read-only SMBIOS/OS/EDAC and approved SPD queries only; do not alter DIMMs or ECC policy.
Treat raw FFFFh as Unknown rather than 65535 bits.
When both values are known, require Total Width not less than Data Width and report their difference explicitly.
Do not infer active ECC correction solely from extra width bits.
Stop on device-identity ambiguity, impossible relationship or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Decode per-device raw total/data widths, validate sentinel and arithmetic relationships, compare approved design and pre/post reboot evidence.
Do not modify memory state, claim live ECC behavior or issue PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve device width/check-bit design, Unknown/empty-slot and SPD-correlation policy.
Approve reboot/recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The Total Width line is relevant, but grep -A1 drops the enclosing locator/identity, raw FFFFh value and may not preserve the paired Data Width for every record.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive complete raw/decoded Type 17 data; report handle/locator/population, raw and decoded Total Width/Data Width, their difference and approved module/SPD comparison.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Total Width scope, Type 17 script and 5/5-minute values are retained; log clearing and ECC/hardware changes are excluded.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Evaluate raw Total Width and Data Width together for every identified Type 17 record, handle FFFFh explicitly, compute check-bit width and compare with the approved memory-device design before and after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 17 memory-device records for populated and represented empty slots.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, BIOS/BMC, dmidecode/parser and optional SPD-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 17 Total Width/Data Width definitions and authoritative module/platform ECC design.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds device identity, raw sentinel semantics, paired-field arithmetic and design correlation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects Unknown misdecoding, total-smaller-than-data defects, wrong check-bit widths and values attached to the wrong socket.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Per-device width/ECC baseline and empty/unknown policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Extra physical width is structural metadata and does not prove ECC is enabled, exercised or correctly reported at runtime.

project_override_considerations: A project may mix ECC and non-ECC device classes, but must define expected widths per locator or approved class; a global 72/64 assumption must not be applied to every technology.
expected_evidence: Approved platform/device identity, total/data/check-bit baseline and Unknown policy
Per-device raw/decoded Total Width and Data Width, difference and structural rule result
Optional trusted SPD/EDAC context labeled by device identity
Approved reboot/health evidence and post-reboot semantic width comparison

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Total Width has defined bit/sentinel semantics and complements the separate Data Width row.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Width decoding and paired-field comparison are fully automatable after the design baseline is provided.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Adds device identity, raw FFFFh, Data Width pairing and explicit check-bit arithmetic.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its safe per-device design correlation while restoring FULLY AUTOMATABLE classification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates structural width evidence from live ECC behavior and engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Prevents a plausible width label from passing when it is Unknown, belongs to another device or contradicts Data Width/check-bit design.
independent_technical_reasoning: Two finite raw width fields and device identities can be exhaustively decoded and compared; baseline approval affects readiness, not the software-executable core.
